name: Samuel Ellis
current_role: Early-stage software investor; partner at Scout Ventures (per 2022 interviews; current status not confirmed)
profile: Sam Ellis is a West Point graduate (operations research) and former Army intelligence officer at U.S. Cyber Command who co-founded Dutchie, the cannabis e-commerce/POS platform later valued at about $3.75B. He built Dutchie's first software version, then moved into venture investing as a partner at Scout Ventures, leading SaaS pre-seed and seed deals.
interesting_fact: He single-handedly wrote the first version of Dutchie's online cannabis marketplace software while coming out of a military cyber role, coding in his spare time.
deep_cut_fact: Before Dutchie he served as a software developer and intelligence leader at U.S. Cyber Command after studying operations research and applied statistics at West Point; he has said he spotted great engineers as people who 'love the game'.
notes: Low public profile; the less-visible co-founder next to Ross and Zach Lipson. Veteran-focused VC (Scout Ventures) is the natural route; current Scout role unverified on its team page. Podcasts: Travis Makes Money #717 (2022), Those Who Dare (May 2022).

name: Pedro Castillo
current_role: Founder of Onum, now Falcon Onum inside CrowdStrike (deal announced Aug 2025, reported ~$290M); co-founder of Devo
profile: Spanish engineer Pedro (del) Castillo co-founded Devo (originally Logtrust) in Madrid in 2011, a cloud-native security data analytics platform that became Spain's first cybersecurity unicorn; he served as CEO and then about 11 years as CTO. In 2022-23 he founded Onum, a real-time security data pipeline company, which CrowdStrike agreed to buy in 2025 to feed its Falcon Next-Gen SIEM.
interesting_fact: CrowdStrike's 2025 purchase of Onum (reported at $290M) gave Castillo a second security exit after Devo; he said pipelines should 'transform data into real-time intelligence', not just move it.
deep_cut_fact: Before Devo he was security tech director, then CTO and head of tech innovation at Bankinter, where back in 2001 his team built an on-prem system to collect all the data the bank generated, the seed of the Devo idea. Devo spent two years building product before launching and came within days of running out of cash.

public_contacts.value: https://www.crowdstrike.com (onum.com now redirects to CrowdStrike's Falcon Onum page)

notes: Also appears as Pedro del Castillo / Pedro Muros Castillo. Since the CrowdStrike deal, CrowdStrike press relations is likely the route; his post-acquisition title not verified. MWC Barcelona speaker. Do not confuse with Peru's former president Pedro Castillo.

name: Alexandre Yazdi
profile: Alexandre Yazdi, an engineering graduate (Polytech Nancy), co-founded Paris-based Voodoo with Laurent Ritter around 2012-13. Voodoo became one of the world's largest mobile game publishers through hyper-casual hits, backed by Goldman Sachs and Tencent at a ~$2B valuation, and has since expanded into consumer apps, including the social apps Wizz and BeReal.
interesting_fact: In June 2024 Voodoo bought French social app BeReal for a headline €500M, with Yazdi saying the aim was to refocus BeReal on growth and add advertising to move it toward profitability.
deep_cut_fact: Voodoo's very first app was a trivia game called 'Quiz Run', which passed 10 million downloads; by early 2016 the company had raised only about €1M in total.
notes: Keeps a fairly low personal media profile; company press office is the cleanest route. Some 2026 reports link him to buying a stake in DC Company (Konbini/Le Gorafi) but that is unverified here.

name: Matt Vincett
current_role: Longtime CEO of LifeMiles / Avianca Chief Loyalty Officer (2010 to at least late 2023); current role unverified after Avianca named new LifeMiles leadership in 2025
profile: Matt Vincett built LifeMiles, the Avianca-TACA frequent-flyer programme, as its CEO from 2010, launching it in March 2011 and leading its 2015 carve-out and partial sale to Advent International at a valuation of about $1B+. Avianca bought the whole business back in 2020. LifeMiles had more than 11 million members in 2023 and earns most of its money selling miles to banks and retailers.
interesting_fact: He describes LifeMiles as a business that sells miles to banks, partners and retailers more than an airline perk; by 2023 it had 11M+ members and co-branded cards in 10 countries.
deep_cut_fact: Before LifeMiles he was an airline man at TACA, serving as Commercial VP, VP of TACA's regional airlines and Director of Strategy & Business Development (per Avianca IR management bio).
notes: In Feb 2025 Avianca named Valeria Yglesias SVP Loyalty & managing director of LifeMiles, and later Jaime Manso to lead LifeMiles, so Vincett has probably moved on; his bio is gone from Avianca's current IR page (the TACA background came from an earlier version). Very low public profile; LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Jonathan Webb
current_role: Co-founder of Pharmapacks (later renamed Packable); co-founder and CEO of Packable per directory profiles; current activity unverified
profile: Jonathan Webb is one of five co-founders of Pharmapacks (2010, New York), which grew from a Bronx pharmacy operation into one of Amazon's largest US third-party sellers of health and beauty products and was valued at about $1B. It was renamed Packable, an e-commerce enablement company, and he is listed as its co-founder and CEO. His background is in spirits and luxury marketing and sales.
interesting_fact: Pharmapacks went from a Bronx retail pharmacy to one of the biggest sellers on Amazon in the US, built by a small group of friends.
deep_cut_fact: Before e-commerce, he co-founded LeSutra, a sparkling liqueur launched in 2012 with music producer Timbaland and Grey Goose co-founder Tom Bruno, with fellow future Pharmapacks co-founder Adam Berkowitz.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Packable (ex-Pharmapacks) went through Chapter 11 in 2022 after a planned SPAC deal fell through, so avoid framing outreach around the company's valuation. LinkedIn is the likely route.
